links.outcome: Agreement rate with wrong AI recommendations (automation bias) and factors associated with it
links.effect: Automation bias occurred and was associated with user factors. Diagnostic performance, wound care training, physician profession and female gender reduced false agreement. Higher perceived system benefit increased it. Non-specialists were most susceptible.
links.quote: This study highlights that non-specialists, who stand to gain the most from CDSS, are also the most susceptible to automation bias, emphasizing the need for specialized training to mitigate this risk and ensure diagnostic accuracy and patient safety.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates factors contributing to automation bias (agreement with incorrect AI recommendations) in a simulated diagnostic task, testing the role of specialized training and professional background.

primary.practice: clinician training and expertise assessment to mitigate automation bias
